title: senecio incanus subsp. carniolicus
intro: Senecio incanus subsp. carniolicus, commonly known as Alpine Ragwort, is a plant species within the daisy family (Asteraceae) native to the mountainous regions of Europe, particularly in the Alps and the Carpathian Mountains. The Alpine Ragwort plant has been traditionally used in folk medicine for its various health benefits, including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, which may help to alleviate symptoms of respiratory issues and improve overall well-being. The therapeutic actions of Senecio incanus subsp. carniolicus include its potential to exhibit anti-inflammatory, antispasmodic, and expectorant properties, making it a promising candidate for treating respiratory and gastrointestinal disorders. Bioactive constituents of this plant include sesquiterpene lactones, such as carniolic acid, and flavonoids, which contribute to its medicinal properties and may provide further research opportunities for its applications in pharmacology and medicine.
